messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for eng-oncall — rule=latency_slo_burn (p95/p99 spike)
PagerDuty: Incident PD-4982 auto-triggered. Escalation policy: eng-oncall. Paging Maya Chen, Jonah Patel.
monitoring-bot: Quick summary — p95=780ms (baseline 220ms), p99=1.3s. QPS +40% on /v1/generate over last 5m. Error rate stable.
Maya Chen: acked. I'm oncall and looking at traces now. Jonah if you can lead mitigation please take it.
Jonah Patel: ack — I'm taking lead. Pulling logs and routing tables. Maya if you need a handoff, ping.
Samir Rao: looking at customer surface: no widespread 5xx increases, but a few client timeouts at ~2s. Early estimate: ~0.9% of requests saw >1s latency, high-tier customers ~0.15%.
Lin Morales: I see increased KV cache miss rate on gpu-pool-02 and batch sizes jumping to 48 for some routes — continuous batching likely over-aggregating due to a traffic burst. Suggest temporary reduce max_batch_size to 16 and enable prefer_small_batches on prod inference config.
Jonah Patel: good call. Applying config change to inference-config/prod — setting max_batch_size: 16 and prefer_small_batches: true. Will push a rolling update to pool tags gpu-pool-02.
Jonah Patel: command I'm running:
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/inference-runtime MAX_BATCH_SIZE=16 PREFER_SMALL_BATCHES=true
# or via config map patch: kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
# (omitted for brevity)
EOF
```
incident-bot: Change applied by Jonah Patel. Notifying autoscaler and runtime.
monitoring-bot: Metrics update (60s after change) — p95=290ms, p99=450ms, CPU steady. Traffic back to expected distribution.
Maya Chen: thanks. Looks like config change brought latency down quickly. Any root cause hypothesis besides traffic burst?
Samir Rao: evidence points to batching policy + cache misses aggravated by a sudden burst from a multi-tenant customer spike. No infra failures. I can correlate client IDs if we need to reach out.
Lin Morales: also noticed an unusually large contiguous sequence of long contexts from some requests, increasing KV pressure. Recommend follow-up: add circuit-breaker for max_batch_time and a guard to drop oversized batching attempts for single-tenant bursts.
Jonah Patel: creating incident ticket INC-2026 and linking the config change PR and the monitoring graphs. I'll own the 30m watch.
Maya Chen: I'll take post-incident ownership: write a short postmortem and add runbook step to check kv cache miss rate + batching flags. Samir, can you collect list of affected customers for outreach?
Samir Rao: on it. Initial list compiled, approx 4 customers with elevated p99s. Will add to the ticket.
Maya Chen: on-call handoff: I'm stepping off at 12:18 UTC — handing to Jonah for the watch. Jonah, if it re-escalates, please page oncall-lead. :thumbsup:
Jonah Patel: confirmed. Monitoring alerts adjusted to temporary threshold. Will escalate if p95 goes above 500ms again for >3min.
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-4982 acknowledged by Maya Chen and Jonah Patel. Escalation suspended.
monitoring-bot: Final snapshot before stabilization: p95 peak=780ms -> back to ~280ms, p99 peak=1.3s -> ~430ms. No sustained error-rate change.
Maya Chen: thanks team. Follow-ups: (1) postmortem + customer outreach (Samir) (2) runbook tweak for batching guard (Lin) (3) add a synthetic test for KV cache pressure (Jonah). I'll assign action items in INC-2026.
Jonah Patel: noted. I'll also add a temporary alert that watches for batch_size > 32 for any pool.
Maya Chen: closing on Slack for now. If anything regresses, re-open PD and call.
incident-bot: PD-4982 marked resolved after metrics stable for 10m.
